speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. Since you are a newborn presenting with respiratory distress, I need to know if this started immediately after birth or if it developed later. Did you have any difficulty breathing during delivery, or were there any complications noted? REQUEST TEST: Arterial_Blood_Gas.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: pH: 7.30 (slightly acidic), PaCO2: 50 mmHg (elevated), PaO2: 60 mmHg (reduced), HCO3-: 24 mEq/L

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Grunting, Intercoastal and subcostal retractions, Peripheral cyanosis. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those specific details; the presence of grunting and retractions suggests significant effort to overcome increased airway resistance. Given your age and symptoms, have you been fed orally, or has feeding been difficult due to this breathing trouble? REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Fine reticular granulation with ground glass appearance on both lungs

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS).
